assumptions: Action Units are used as an observable facial-motion vocabulary.
confidence_basis: The source is preserved and hash-verified, but no qualified immutable experiment evidence establishes provider-general performance.
constraints: Do not infer private internal state from visible activation.
Do not collapse meaningful asymmetry into one bilateral scalar.
failure_conditions: The prompt specifies only an emotion label with no observable facial action.
Onset, apex, or offset timing is lost.
limitations: The current universal score control stores Action Unit identities but does not yet serialize the complete temporal curve.
name: Temporal Action Unit event encoding

review.notes: Owner explicitly requested source-closed population of claims, equations, methods, and mechanisms. This review authorizes normalization of the exact preserved CPCS section; records remain ingested and unverified and do not establish provider or scientific qualification.

source_evidence.claim: The method is a bounded operational normalization of the preserved section’s baseline, laterality, timing, and confidence requirements.

purpose: Encode a facial performance as source-traceable bilateral Action Unit events rather than one static emotion label.
steps: Select the visible Action Units relevant to the intended performance.
Represent left and right intensities independently when asymmetry matters.
Specify onset, apex, and offset over time.
Attach a confidence or constraint weight and preserve uncertainty.
